def clear(self) -> None:
        """Reset the list of log records and the captured log text."""
        self.handler.reset()
        # ``reset`` replaces the records list, so the per-stage reference
        # stashed in ``_runtest_for`` would otherwise diverge from
        # ``self.records``. Keep them pointing at the same object so that
        # ``get_records`` stays consistent with ``records``.
        records = self._item.stash[caplog_records_key]
        records[self._item.stash[caplog_handler_key].records is not None and self._current_stage()] = (
            self.handler.records
        )

arguments.message:
Fix caplog.get_records/caplog.records divergence after caplog.clear().

Issue: `_runtest_for` stores `caplog_handler.records` in `item.stash[caplog_records_key][when]` (returned by `get_records`), but `LogCaptureFixture.clear()` delegated to `LogCaptureHandler.reset()`, which did `self.records = []` — replacing the list object. The stashed per-stage reference kept pointing at the old list, so `get_records("call")` stopped tracking `caplog.records` and became frozen (neither cleared nor receiving new records).

Change (src/_pytest/logging.py): `LogCaptureFixture.clear()` now clears the existing list in place (`self.handler.records.clear()`) and resets the stream, instead of calling `reset()`. The per-stage boundary `reset()` in `_runtest_for` is unchanged, so stages still get fresh lists while any external reference to `records` (including the stashed one) stays identical to `caplog.records`.

Verification (v13, same-version public tests): testing/logging/test_fixture.py — 15 passed, 0 failed, including test_clear and test_caplog_captures_for_all_stages.
